content.text: So far only seen on Ubuntu 20.10
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: double lock of a mutex (pid=3131387)
because applied too often and way insufficient for hte bug/issue
SUMMARY: ThreadSanitizer: double lock of a mutex (/home/lewis/Sandbox/Stroika-Build-Dir-Ubuntu2010_x86_64/Builds/g++-debug-sanitize_thread/Tests/Test37+0xe274cc) in __interceptor_pthread_mutex_lock
Write of size 1 at 0x7b58000003d8 by thread T1 (mutexes: write M400393034769892224):
Previous read of size 1 at 0x7b58000003d8 by main thread (mutexes: write M400393034769892224):
Location is heap block of size 680 at 0x7b5800000300 allocated by main thread:
and I looked at the code and I cannot see off hand how this can be a double lock. I considered clearing memory issue (block allocation) but happens in many configs and the memory alloc is make_shared

And the set() code in question really looks like it cannot lock twice. And very few references to that object. Tehre COULD be a bug with the condition varaible code causing it to get locked multiple times, but its more likely tsan is getting confused.
